skill.name: sqlmodel-crud
skill.description: Provides guidance for building SQLModel table classes, async CRUD operations, joined queries, relationships, database setup, and migration structure for FastAPI-style projects.
skill.summary: Guides SQLModel model, CRUD, relationship, query, and migration scaffolding for Python backend projects.
skill.author: Awais68

security_audit.summary: AI review found the static command, network, environment, and reconnaissance hits are documentation or example false positives. The file contains SQLModel snippets, SQLAlchemy query examples, normal DATABASE_URL configuration, and reference links, with no prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: The database setup example includes a placeholder fallback URL.
remediation.suggestion: Require DATABASE_URL from the environment and avoid sample credentials in reusable production-oriented examples.

remediation.issue: The SQLAlchemy engine example enables echo logging unconditionally.
remediation.suggestion: Gate SQL echo logging behind a development setting so generated production code does not log sensitive query data.

- Return `Optional[T]` for single items, `List[T]` for lists
- [ ] **Eager loading**: Use selectinload for relationship access

content.value_statement: Designing SQLModel models and CRUD code can be slow when relationships and async sessions are involved. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through models, queries, relationships, and database setup.
actual_capabilities: Designs SQLModel table classes with fields, indexes, validators, timestamps, and relationships.
Creates async CRUD methods using AsyncSession, select queries, pagination, and transactions.
Builds joined queries, search filters, aggregation summaries, and eager loading patterns.
Models one-to-many, many-to-many, one-to-one, and self-referential relationships.
Outlines database setup, session dependency patterns, and Alembic migration imports.
limitations: Does not inspect a live database schema or run migrations.
Requires user-provided entity names, fields, constraints, and relationship rules.
Examples assume Python SQLModel, SQLAlchemy async sessions, and FastAPI-style projects.
Generated code still needs project-specific tests, authorization checks, and migration review.

use_cases.title: Create ERP Models
use_cases.description: Define Student, Fee, Attendance, and Class tables with validators and relationships.

use_cases.title: Add Async CRUD
use_cases.description: Generate create, read, update, delete, count, and filtered list methods for SQLModel tables.

use_cases.title: Plan Query Logic
use_cases.description: Draft joined queries, eager loading, search, aggregation, and pagination for reporting screens.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one SQLModel table.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this SQLModel CRUD skill. Create a Student model with name, email, phone, timestamps, and validation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Add CRUD Methods
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for async database operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to write async CRUD methods for my Fee model. Include create, get by id, update, delete, pagination, and transaction handling.

prompt_templates.title: Model Relationships
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced schema request with several linked entities.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design Student, Parent, Class, Fee, and Attendance relationships. Include one-to-many, many-to-many, indexes, and back_populates choices.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Reporting Queries
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for reporting and performance patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design advanced SQLModel queries for attendance and fee reports. Include joins, aggregations, eager loading, filters, and pagination.

output_examples.input: Request: create Student and Class SQLModel models.
output: A model plan with fields, indexes, validators, and timestamps.
Relationship guidance for linking students to classes.
Review notes for uniqueness constraints and foreign keys.

output_examples.input: Request: build CRUD methods for Fee records.
output: An async CRUD outline covering creation, lookup, updates, deletion, and pagination.
Transaction handling notes for commits, refreshes, rollbacks, and returned values.
Testing reminders for missing records and invalid foreign keys.

output_examples.output: The skill returns a query plan covering date filters, joins, aggregation metrics, eager loading, and pagination considerations.

best_practices: Provide entity fields, constraints, and relationship cardinality before asking for model code.
Ask for migration notes and tests when the generated schema changes.
Review generated database defaults, logging, and indexes before production use.
anti_patterns: Using the sample database URL as a production credential.
Generating CRUD methods without authorization or tenant checks.
Adding relationships without confirming cascade behavior and migration impact.

faq.question: Does this skill run database commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users must run migrations or application code themselves.

faq.question: Can it support FastAPI projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include async sessions and database dependency patterns often used with FastAPI.

faq.question: Does it create Alembic migrations?
faq.answer: It outlines migration imports and commands, but migration files still need project review.

faq.question: Can it design relationships?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers foreign keys, back_populates, link tables, one-to-one links, and self-referential relationships.

faq.question: Does it validate user input?
faq.answer: It recommends SQLModel and Pydantic field constraints. Application-specific validation still belongs in your codebase.

faq.question: Is it limited to school ERP entities?
faq.answer: No. Student, Fee, Class, and Attendance are examples that can be adapted to other domains.
